body: fwiw, I ran the script locally over merge commits and https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/39390 was the last one that caused it to fail

Thanks for the reproduction script. It definitely looks like a bug in rails and you have pointed to the right change as reverting the commit works fine.
I will try to provide a fix for this, and hope that this could be fixed without reverting if possible.

The below changes seems to have fixed the issue reported (not sure about the fix though).
```diff
diff --git a/activerecord/lib/active_record/associations/association_scope.rb b/activerecord/lib/active_record/associations/association_scope.rb
index 8f2c6f269c..cdc854492e 100644
--- a/activerecord/lib/active_record/associations/association_scope.rb
+++ b/activerecord/lib/active_record/associations/association_scope.rb
@@ -130,7 +130,7 @@ def add_constraints(scope, owner, chain)
 
               if scope_chain_item == chain_head.scope
                 scope.merge! item.except(:where, :includes, :unscope, :order)
-              elsif !item.references_values.empty?
+              elsif item.references_values.present? && chain_head.scope.present?
                 join_dependency = item.construct_join_dependency(
                   item.eager_load_values | item.includes_values, Arel::Nodes::OuterJoin
                 )

```

Though I notice that the PR #39390 mentions fixing #33525 in master, however the script in the description of  #33525 fails on `master` and `6-0-stable` both with
```ruby
ActiveRecord::ConfigurationError: Can't join 'User' to association named 'source'; perhaps you misspelled it?
```
Note that with the change suggested above #33525 will fail with
```ruby
ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid: SQLite3::SQLException: no such column: sources.online
```

Hey @KapilSachdev, did you get anywhere with this? Since the original bug that was intended to be fixed seems to still be around, seems ok to start a PR with your changes, though I'm sure there are other consequences I don't know about 😄. I've tried throwing a debugger and trying to figure it out but I seem to be a bit out of my depth here.

Combined tests after @KapilSachdev 's changes:

FYI: I rewrote my example to:
```ruby
class Account < ApplicationRecord
  scope :not_suspended, -> { where(suspended_at: nil) }
end

class ApiToken < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :user
  
  scope :active, -> { where(revoked_at: nil).joins(:account).merge(Account.not_suspended) }
end
```
and it works. It is also a bit nicer this way.

issue.title: Fix through association with through scope which has joins
issue.body:
Follow up to #39390.

#39390 works only for through scope with includes, joins are incorrectly
merged if source association and through association are based on
different klass.

Use `scope.merge` to avoid the merging scope issue.

Fixes #40220.

body:
It looks like this was fixed in the 6.1 release but is still broken on the 6.0 release series, including in the security update 6.0.4.1 - would it be possible to backport the fix to the 6.0 branch as well? https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/41029

Based on a number of tests in our test suite that result in the same error as in this issue it looks like 6.0.4 introduces the issue, same tests pass on 6.0.3.7 and 6.1.4.1 though
